articles.titleTr: Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks
articles.summaryTr: The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC.
articles.articleText: Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC. US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation. The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission. The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks. Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill Levine, a Republican, was nominated for an SEC term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Peirce, who left the agency in October. Peirce was a leading advocate for clearer crypto rules at the SEC, helping shape its approach to digital assets as the former head of its Crypto Task Force, while Levine’s views on crypto regulation are less publicly established. Trump also nominated Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, for the SEC seat held by Caroline Crenshaw, whose term has also expired. Johnson’s proposed term ends June 5, 2029. Johnson has advocated for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules for crypto firms in her time at the CFTC. For the CFTC, Trump nominated Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC Chairman Mike Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” for CFTC commissioners and said he looked forward to working with them upon their confirmation. The nominees would typically appear before the Senate Banking Committee for the SEC positions and the Senate Agriculture Committee for the CFTC roles. Following committee consideration, their nominations would go to the full Senate, where confirmation requires a majority vote. Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill Levine, a Republican, was nominated for an SEC term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Peirce, who left the agency in October. Peirce was a leading advocate for clearer crypto rules at the SEC, helping shape its approach to digital assets as the former head of its Crypto Task Force, while Levine’s views on crypto regulation are less publicly established. Trump also nominated Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, for the SEC seat held by Caroline Crenshaw, whose term has also expired. Johnson’s proposed term ends June 5, 2029. Johnson has advocated for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules for crypto firms in her time at the CFTC. For the CFTC, Trump nominated Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC Chairman Mike Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” for CFTC commissioners and said he looked forward to working with them upon their confirmation. The nominees would typically appear before the Senate Banking Committee for the SEC positions and the Senate Agriculture Committee for the CFTC roles. Following committee consideration, their nominations would go to the full Senate, where confirmation requires a majority vote. Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? articles.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
articles.summary: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.

articles.titleTr: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
articles.summaryTr: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
articles.articleText: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks - Published Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia. European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations. Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed. The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war. But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but further details like how many prisoners would be exchanged or a timeline, were not given. - US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow - Published11 hours ago - Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine - Published17 hours ago Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union. On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important." He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it is to have European delegates "at the table". "He's willing to give it a try," Kushner added. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Earlier on Thursday, Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, told BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player". Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal. Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of Euro leaders gathered in the Irish capital on Thursday that he believed the security of the region has been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war. "Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine remains under control of Russian forces, and cross-border incursions are increasingly common. Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky. Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The technology owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company has played a vital role in government and military connectivity in Ukraine, and increasingly assists in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

articles.title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters
articles.summary: Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters
articles.summaryTr: Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO.
articles.articleText: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, Reuters reported, bringing the number of alleged extramarital affairs to three. The report, citing two people familiar with the matter, followed Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO and a board member on Thursday. Reuters did not identify the other employee in its report and said attempts to reach her were unsuccessful. The two previously reported relationships involved Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of working for Chinese intelligence, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Cointelegraph reached out to Nvidia for comment. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday during a press conference that the Justice Department had not determined whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. He confirmed that the FBI was investigating reports that she worked for the Chinese government. Beijing has denied the allegations. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance. Venture capitalist Haseeb Qureshi argued that the mounting disclosures undermined Huang’s credibility, pushing back against tech industry figures defending the Nvidia co-founder. “As others have said: ‘when you find two ants in your kitchen, the best estimate for the ants in your kitchen is not two,’” Qureshi wrote on X. Related: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge

articles.title: Burnham says 'win-win' deal can be agreed between UK and EU
articles.summary: The prime minister says the deal could be "more like the Brexit people thought they were voting for" in 2016.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Burnham says 'win-win' deal can be agreed between UK and EU
articles.summaryTr: The prime minister says the deal could be "more like the Brexit people thought they were voting for" in 2016.
articles.articleText: Burnham says 'win-win' deal can be agreed between UK and EU - Published Andy Burnham said he believes a "win-win" deal can be agreed with the European Union, adding it could be "more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for" in 2016. The prime minister is exploring closer ties with the bloc and is expected to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility at a UK-EU summit on 20 November. Speaking after meeting European leaders in Ireland on Thursday, Burnham said he hopes a deal could help lower prices and boost the UK economy. He predicted the negotiations could "go down to the wire". The Conservatives have previously said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door with their EU reset". While Burnham has argued that Brexit has done "more harm than good", he has ruled out major changes to the UK's relationship with the EU before the next general election. Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledged there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement", and Burnham has committed to this. The manifesto also said the party wanted to "make Brexit work" and reset the UK's relationship with the EU. Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer struck a deal in May 2025 covering fishing, trade and other areas and next week's summit will see the UK government seek to agree further changes. Burnham has also made clear he wants to examine the "pros and cons" of the options for Britain's long-term relationship with the bloc. - Burnham's push for closer EU ties causes ripples in his party and others - Published1 day ago - UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC - Published5 days ago - Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, says Burnham - Published30 September - Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion? - Published14 hours ago Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Burnham was asked to explain if his decision to reopen the debate on the UK's future with Europe had helped or hindered the negotiations linked to the summit. Burnham replied "I think it has helped" before adding: "We've got a big week ahead of us to try and get this deal over the line. "But let's be clear what's at stake: what we can achieve through this deal is lower prices for British consumers, lower costs for British businesses, more growth in our economy so there's really big prizes here, and I will fight now over the days to come to make sure we get this deal over the line." Pressed on whether discounted university tuition fees for European students would be part of the deal, Burnham said "requests are coming from the European side, we are putting our requests on the table too". He added: "I believe there is a good deal to be done that could be a win-win for Britain and Europe. I think it actually could be more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for in 2016." Ahead of the summit, the UK and EU agreed a draft deal on removing post-Brexit checks from food and agriculture exports. Similar texts for deals on emissions trading and a youth travel and work scheme have also been circulated to EU nations. As a result of the agreement, the government claims the UK economy will eventually see £5.1bn worth of annual benefits. Burnham also told MPs last month that the summit presents an opportunity to make progress on "controlling illegal immigration". Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has previously strongly opposed any move to align with EU rules, saying it would "actually take us backwards". On Thursday, Conservative MP and former minister Dame Priti Patel said: "Andy Burnham's obsession with the EU risks dragging Britain backwards, damaging our economy and leaving hardworking British taxpayers footing the bill." The Liberal Democrats earlier this month described the draft deal as a "patch, not a fix" and said the "real solution is to re-join the single market and to establish a customs union with the EU". Reform UK believes one of the "key benefits" of Brexit is that Britain no longer has to "adhere to ridiculous EU rules" and any form of alignment could have a negative impact on the country's trade policy. The Green Party has called for the UK to re-join the customs union, with leader Zack Polanski previously saying "full membership of the EU remains the best option for the UK". articles.title: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low
articles.summary: Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low
articles.summaryTr: Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump.
articles.articleText: Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump. Crypto exchange Gemini has just reported its lowest quarterly retail trading volume in three years, despite an increase in overall crypto trading volume. Total spot trading volume rose 18% from the second quarter to $4.5 billion, according to Gemini’s Q3 earnings report. Institutional volume climbed 26% to $3.9 billion, while retail volume fell 14% to $600 million, its lowest level since the third quarter of 2023. Gemini said the quarterly increase in spot trading volume was “supported by increased institutional Zcash activity and expanded affiliated market-making,” but did not give a specific reason for the decline in retail trading. Despite the retail slump, Gemini’s exchange revenue increased 7% from the previous quarter to $13.4 million as institutional revenue more than doubled. Retail traders remained its largest source of exchange revenue, contributing nearly three-quarters of the total. Crypto exchanges turn to prediction markets for growth A number of crypto exchanges also reported softer crypto trading activity in the most recent quarter. Coinbase reported softer retail and institutional activity, with consumer spot trading volume falling 9% from the previous quarter to $23.4 billion. Coinbase chief financial officer Alesia Haas said “continued growth in prediction markets helped offset softer crypto trading activity.” At Robinhood, crypto revenue fell 55% year-on-year to $120 million, offset by a sixfold increase in event-contract revenue to $173 million. Related: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off Gemini also got some help from its own prediction exchange, Gemini Predictions, with revenue from that business unit increasing 52% quarter-on-quarter to $796,000, though it wasn’t significant enough to offset declines elsewhere. Gemini looks to expand prediction markets Gemini reported stronger prediction-market activity heading into the fourth quarter, with average daily traders in October running about 50% above the third-quarter average. Nearly a third of new prediction traders were new to Gemini, more than double the proportion in Q3. The company is also seeking to distribute its event contracts through other platforms. An August nonbinding agreement with Apex Fintech Solutions would make Gemini Titan the exclusive venue for crypto event contracts distributed through Apex’s futures brokerage to its brokerage customers, subject to definitive agreements. Gemini is set to host a Q3 earnings call on Friday. Magazine: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express

articles.title: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
articles.summary: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
articles.summaryTr: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
articles.articleText: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over? - Published Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment. "People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC. After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter. "Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion. Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next." Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022. But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force. Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements. Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority. Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat. "The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage." Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says. Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost. Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC. He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy." The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability. It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored. Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes. Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days. "We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active. Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents. The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds. Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded. Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC. Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations. However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael. Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF." He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says. Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says. What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded." While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours." In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict. "First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF." Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade. Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement. Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government. However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence. In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace. "Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle. articles.title: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
articles.summary: Experts warn that using AI to enhance property images can go too far and mislead prospective buyers.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
articles.summaryTr: Experts warn that using AI to enhance property images can go too far and mislead prospective buyers.
articles.articleText: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading? - Published Have you ever been impressed by the pictures of a property on an estate agent's website, only to find the place looks completely different when you view it in person? Then there's a chance that AI was used to enhance the images you saw. From repainted walls to imaginary lawns, estate agents are increasingly using the technology to make homes seem more appealing, arguing it helps buyers visualise the potential of a place. But experts warn it can go too far and mislead prospective buyers - a trend dubbed "housefishing". So how much AI enhancement is too much? 'The rooms were much smaller' Earlier this year Olivia Nicole, 29, was searching online for five-bedroom properties in south-west London when a house on Rightmove caught her eye. But when she arrived to view it several days later she initially thought she had come to the wrong place. "The rooms were much smaller than they were in the pictures and the decor was totally different," she tells the BBC. "Some structural features were also different." For example, there was a raised section of the wall behind the sofa that didn't appear in the images. The windows were also noticeably smaller. Olivia was so surprised she took her own pictures of the property for comparison. It later turned out the pictures she had seen on Rightmove, which also appeared on the Zoopla and Winkworth websites, were enhanced with AI. But that wasn't clear in the listing, Olivia says, and she feels the agent wasted her time. "It was frustrating, because I had taken several hours off work for the viewing which I had to make up for." All three companies told the BBC they had strict guidelines on how AI could be used on their websites and have since taken the images down. 'A surge of AI listings' Estate agents have long used wide-angle lens cameras or Photoshop to make homes seem bigger or more appealing to buyers, but AI is making this process much easier and more accessible. It is difficult to quantify how common the practice is, says the Guild of Property Professionals, a trade group of independent estate agents, but it has issued guidance on how to use AI enhancement responsibly. According to a recent survey, external of 906 UK homebuyers, one in five who had who purchased a home in the past year said they had viewed a property where the listing photos had been digitally enhanced to make the home appear better than it actually was. Jack Bushrod reviews quirky property listings he finds on Rightmove for his social media channel, Housing Horrors, and says he has seen a "surge" of AI-enhanced images over the last six months. He thinks using AI is fine up to a point - to declutter a busy room, or add furniture to an empty one so a prospective buyer can see its potential. But he draws the line at anything that misleads a prospective buyer or wastes their time. "I've seen one house where they had removed a pillar and added a window. Others might use AI to remove stains on the carpet or cracks in tiles. It's little details you would only notice in person." He says most of the enhanced images he's seen weren't clearly labelled as AI-generated. Cara, 38, is currently selling her home in Lowestoft, Suffolk, and says she was surprised when she saw the AI-enhanced pictures of her property her estate agent, Howards, put on Rightmove. In one photo, her son's room was completely emptied of toys and clutter. In another, of her daughter's room, the agent appears to have removed a doll's house, brightened the room, and used AI to change the shape of a rug, but that image has since been taken down. Cara has had several viewings so far and says that one person has commented on the differences. But she says she trusts Howards, which has acknowledged the use of AI in the property listing. "If they'd changed something structurally or it was really wild and didn't look like our home at all then I would put my foot down," she says. A spokeswoman told the BBC that Howards had now introduced a policy of labelling all AI-enhanced photos. She added that the firm never used AI "to misrepresent the fundamental features of a property". "It's about helping people imagine the possibilities, not changing the reality of what's being sold." 'Jumping on the bandwagon' Trading Standards told the BBC that estate agents can use AI to make basic enhancements to photos, or to virtually furnish an empty room or garden, as long as they indicate they have used the technology. But it says structurally changing a room, for example by adding a window, or hiding features could mislead consumers and break the law. Jack Bushrod thinks all estate agents should have to clearly label AI-enhanced photos and mention any use of the tech prominently in the key features slide of a property listing. He also expects to see more housefishing as time goes on. "My worry is the more estate agents use AI, others will see the trend and jump on the bandwagon." articles.articleText: Military cemetery decorum: The tradition behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand Earlier this week, a sentinel reprimanded a group that included US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery. The incident followed a wreath-laying ceremony marking Veterans Day. The Pentagon have since announced that Hegseth has given the soldier, Specialist Thomas Iglesias, a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier". BBC's Bernd Debusmann breaks down why Hegseth's group was reprimanded, the history behind the strict rules governing visitor behaviour and the importance of maintaining an atmosphere of silence at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

articles.title: Maple Finance’s strategy rift sends co-founder, COO to the exits
articles.summary: Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth.

articles.titleTr: Maple Finance’s strategy rift sends co-founder, COO to the exits
articles.summaryTr: Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth.
articles.articleText: Maple Finance’s strategy rift sends co-founder, COO to the exits Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth. Two senior executives are leaving onchain asset manager Maple Finance over disagreements about the firm’s direction as its SYRUP token slid more than 7% Thursday. Maple co-founder and executive chairman Joe Flanagan said Wednesday he would leave after seven years at the firm, describing a growing divide with fellow co-founder and CEO Sidney Powell. “Over time, our views on strategy, leadership, and life have moved further apart,” Flanagan wrote. “I believe Maple is best served by one co-founder leading it forward from here.” Chief operating officer Ryan O’Shea also said in a Thursday post on X that he would leave after nearly five years at Maple. “I’ll be stepping down as COO. I’ve come to a different view on the direction Maple should take, and I’ve decided it’s time to step aside,” he wrote. SYRUP traded at $0.12 at 10:36 p.m. UTC Thursday, down 7.5% over 24 hours and 12% over the past week, according to CoinGecko. The token had a market capitalization of about $145 million. Maple and Powell did not respond to Cointelegraph’s requests for comment by publication. Maple says leadership shakeup will not disrupt anything In a statement published Wednesday, Maple confirmed that Flanagan was stepping down as chairman and leaving the company. “This is an agreed and orderly transition,” the company said, adding that his responsibilities would move to Powell and Maple’s existing leadership team. The company did not announce a replacement chairman or specify how the departing executives’ duties would be carried out. Flanagan said his differences with Powell reached a point where they were no longer constructive. “I am choosing to leave rather than continue supporting a direction I cannot stand behind,” he said. Flanagan added that he would help with the transition through the end of 2026. O’Shea is stepping down effective Nov. 27. “I’ll have no ongoing role after that,” he wrote. The departures come as Maple looks to expand beyond crypto-backed lending. In October, Powell said the firm planned to reach more customers through fintech partnerships and lend against a wider range of assets, including payments owed on loans made by fintech companies and securities backed by assets such as mortgages. Related: Kraken, Maple launch onchain warehouse facility for crypto-backed institutional loans Revenue growth continues The announcements come as Maple’s lending business continues to grow, while SYRUP is down 62% year to date and total value locked (TVL) has declined. According to Token Terminal, Maple’s protocol revenue rose 8% year over year in October, while TVL fell around 11% between the end of September and Nov. 11. Maple’s latest quarterly results also showed growth, with the company reporting $4.4 million in third-quarter revenue, up 5% from a year earlier. Assets under management rose 18% year over year to $4.7 billion. Maple has also been using some of its revenue to buy back SYRUP tokens. In September, the company repurchased about 1.37 million tokens, twice as many as in August, according to its October update. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

SYRUP traded at $0.12 at 10:36 p.m. UTC Thursday, down 7.5% over 24 hours and 12% over the past week, according to CoinGecko. The token had a market capitalization of about $145 million. Maple and Powell did not respond to Cointelegraph’s requests for comment by publication. Maple says leadership shakeup will not disrupt anything In a statement published Wednesday, Maple confirmed that Flanagan was stepping down as chairman and leaving the company. “This is an agreed and orderly transition,” the company said, adding that his responsibilities would move to Powell and Maple’s existing leadership team. The company did not announce a replacement chairman or specify how the departing executives’ duties would be carried out. Flanagan said his differences with Powell reached a point where they were no longer constructive. “I am choosing to leave rather than continue supporting a direction I cannot stand behind,” he said. Flanagan added that he would help with the transition through the end of 2026. O’Shea is stepping down effective Nov. 27. “I’ll have no ongoing role after that,” he wrote. The departures come as Maple looks to expand beyond crypto-backed lending. In October, Powell said the firm planned to reach more customers through fintech partnerships and lend against a wider range of assets, including payments owed on loans made by fintech companies and securities backed by assets such as mortgages. Related: Kraken, Maple launch onchain warehouse facility for crypto-backed institutional loans Revenue growth continues The announcements come as Maple’s lending business continues to grow, while SYRUP is down 62% year to date and total value locked (TVL) has declined. According to Token Terminal, Maple’s protocol revenue rose 8% year over year in October, while TVL fell around 11% between the end of September and Nov. 11. Maple’s latest quarterly results also showed growth, with the company reporting $4.4 million in third-quarter revenue, up 5% from a year earlier. Assets under management rose 18% year over year to $4.7 billion. Maple has also been using some of its revenue to buy back SYRUP tokens. In September, the company repurchased about 1.37 million tokens, twice as many as in August, according to its October update. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

articles.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.titleTr: COP31'de gözler finansmana çevrildi: Türkiye için fırsatlar neler?
news.summaryTr: Mahfi Eğilmez ve Servet Yıldırım, Sesli Ekonomi’nin 83. bölümünde COP31 İklim Zirvesi’ni değerlendirdi. İklim finansmanında 300 milyar dolarlık hedefi masaya yatıran ikili, Türkiye’nin enerji dönüşümündeki konumunu ve yeşil yatırımların ekonomiye sağlayacağı fırsatları ele aldı.
news.articleText: COP31'de gözler finansmana çevrildi: Türkiye için fırsatlar neler? - Mahfi Eğilmez ve Servet Yıldırım, Sesli Ekonomi’nin 83. bölümünde COP31 İklim Zirvesi’ni değerlendirdi. İklim finansmanında 300 milyar dolarlık hedefi masaya yatıran ikili, Türkiye’nin enerji dönüşümündeki konumunu ve yeşil yatırımların ekonomiye sağlayacağı fırsatları ele aldı. Ekonomist Mahfi Eğilmez ve CNBC-e Genel Yayın Yönetmeni Servet Yıldırım, Sesli Ekonomi’nin 83. bölümünde Antalya’da düzenlenen COP31 İklim Zirvesi’ni ve yeşil dönüşümün ekonomiye etkilerini değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Geçmiş iklim zirvelerinde belirlenen hedeflerin ne ölçüde hayata geçirildiğini ele alan Eğilmez ve Yıldırım, iklim finansmanında yeterli ilerleme sağlanamadığına dikkat çekti. Gelişmekte olan ülkelere yönelik iklim finansmanının 2035 yılına kadar en az 300 milyar dolara çıkarılması hedefi de programın gündemindeydi. Türkiye’nin enerji dönüşümünde önemli mesafe katettiğini belirten Yıldırım, yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarının bütçe ve ödemeler dengesi açısından sağlayacağı avantajlara değindi. Eğilmez ise iklim hedeflerinin hayata geçirilmesi için şirketlerin ve ülkelerin taahhütlerinin denetlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Programda Türk şirketlerinin yeşil dönüşüm yatırımları, bankaların sürdürülebilir finansman politikaları ve Z kuşağının tüketim tercihlerinin şirketler üzerindeki etkileri de konuşuldu. Eğilmez ve Yıldırım, COP31’in başarısının verilen sözlerin somut yatırımlara ve uygulamalara dönüşmesiyle ölçüleceğine dikkat çekti.

news.title: Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide
news.summary: Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide
news.summaryTr: Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude.
news.articleText: Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude. A global Microsoft 365 outage continued into Friday, disrupting Outlook email and some Teams features. MicroSoft said in a 7:25 am UTC update that a patch had improved stability on some servers and that it was working to deploy the fix more widely. The update, republished by the University of Pennsylvania, gave no timetable for restoration. The outage began Thursday, leaving some users unable to access their Exchange Online mailboxes. Microsoft said a process that handles secure connection became overloaded, causing affected servers to stop processing requests. The company said it attempted to restore services by restarting infrastructure, redirecting network traffic and expanding server capacity. Microsoft said there was no indication of a security breach. The outage also affected features in Microsoft Copilot and Defender for Office 365. In Teams, users had trouble scheduling meetings and sending invitations. Microsoft said most Teams calls and chats continued to work. Businesses and government agencies worldwide use Microsoft 365 for email and scheduling. Microsoft reported more than 450 million paid commercial seats for the suite in an October filing. Exchange Online hosts the mailboxes and calendars those organizations use, and outside apps, including AI assistants, rely on the same service to retrieve that data when users connect their work accounts. OpenAI reported errors in ChatGPT’s Microsoft 365 connector. Anthropic said the outage caused most email, calendar and search requests through Calude’s Microsoft 365 connector to fail. The US Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit said its clerk’s office could neither send nor receive email for much of Thursday. Japan’s Finance Ministry said it was unable to receive email on Friday and Singapore’s Government Technology Agency told CNA that government email was among systems affected. Türk şirketlerinin Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklarla buluşturulması ve ortak yatırım imkanlarının geliştirilmesi için çalışmalar sürüyor.

news.titleTr: Savunma sanayisinde Türkiye-Suudi Arabistan temasları: Üç yılda 75'in üzerinde toplantı
news.summaryTr: Savunma Sanayii Başkanı Haluk Görgün, Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasında son üç yılda 75'in üzerinde savunma sanayisi toplantısı yapıldığını açıkladı. Türk şirketlerinin Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklarla buluşturulması ve ortak yatırım imkanlarının geliştirilmesi için çalışmalar sürüyor.
news.articleText: Savunma sanayisinde Türkiye-Suudi Arabistan temasları: Üç yılda 75'in üzerinde toplantı - Savunma Sanayii Başkanı Haluk Görgün, Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasında son üç yılda 75'in üzerinde savunma sanayisi toplantısı yapıldığını açıkladı. Türk şirketlerinin Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklarla buluşturulması ve ortak yatırım imkanlarının geliştirilmesi için çalışmalar sürüyor. Cumhurbaşkanlığı Savunma Sanayii Başkanı Haluk Görgün, Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasında savunma sanayisi alanındaki işbirliğini geliştirmek amacıyla son üç yılda 75'i aşkın toplantı gerçekleştirdiklerini, Türk şirketlerinin Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklarla bir araya getirilmesine yönelik çalışmaların sürdüğünü bildirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Dış Ekonomik İlişkiler Kurulu (DEİK), SAHA İstanbul ve Suudi Arabistan Askeri Sanayileri (SAMI) tarafından 11-12 Kasım'da İstanbul'da düzenlenen Türkiye-Suudi Arabistan Savunma Sanayii Günleri kapsamında Görgün, AA muhabirine açıklamalarda bulundu. Görgün, Türkiye'nin savunma sanayisinde özellikle son 20 yılda önemli bir tecrübe kazandığını belirterek, bu birikimi dost ve müttefik ülkelerle paylaşmak üzere farklı seviyelerde işbirliği görüşmeleri yürüttüklerini söyledi. Suudi Arabistan'ın Türkiye'nin kardeş ve iyi müttefik ülkelerinden biri olduğunu vurgulayan Görgün, iki ülke arasında savunma sanayisindeki tecrübenin paylaşılması amacıyla toplantılar, görüşmeler ve koordinasyon çalışmaları yapıldığını ifade etti. Görgün, bu temasların yaygınlaştırılmasının, son kullanıcılarla irtibat kurulmasının ve işbirliğinin farklı alanlara taşınmasının önemine işaret ederek, çalışmaların tedarik, araştırma-geliştirme, insan kaynağının geliştirilmesi ve program yönetimi gibi başlıkları kapsadığını kaydetti. Suudi Arabistan'ın 2030 Vizyonu kapsamında 2018'de kurduğu Askeri Sanayiler Genel Otoritesinin (GAMI), felsefe ve işlev bakımından Türkiye'deki Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığına benzer bir yapıda oluşturulduğunu aktaran Görgün, aynı dönemde şirketlerin faaliyetleri için Suudi Arabistan Askeri Sanayileri (SAMI) ve araştırma-geliştirme süreçlerini yönetmek üzere Savunma Geliştirme Genel Otoritesinin (GADD) kurulduğunu belirtti. Görgün, Türkiye'nin Suudi Arabistan'daki bu kurumların tamamıyla etkileşim içinde çalışmalar yürüttüğünü dile getirerek, şöyle devam etti: "Türk şirketlerimizi Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklarla buluşturacak programlar oluşturuyoruz. Araştırma-geliştirme, insan kapasitesinin artırılması, yetenek ve yetkinliklerin oluşturulması, altyapıların ve araştırma programlarının yönetilmesi, program ve alım süreçlerinin iyileştirilmesi ile ortak yatırım alanlarının belirlenmesi konusunda kapsamlı görüşmelerimiz devam ediyor." "Türk firmalarımızı yerel ortaklarla buluşturacak programlar oluşturuyoruz" Türk savunma sanayisi şirketlerinin Suudi Arabistan pazarında sürdürülebilir ortaklıklar kurmasına yönelik çalışmaların halihazırda yürütüldüğünü belirten Görgün, bu kapsamda öncelikle GAMI ve Suudi Arabistan Savunma Bakanlığı ile yoğun temas halinde olduklarını bildirdi. Gördün, Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığı aracılığıyla Türk şirketlerini Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklar ve yerel kapasiteyle buluşturacak programlar oluşturduklarını aktararak, bu alanda hayata geçirilmiş başarılı örneklerin bulunduğunu söyledi. Savunma sanayisinin yüksek teknolojiye dayalı ve geniş bir faaliyet alanına sahip olduğunu vurgulayan Görgün, Türk şirketlerinin farklı alanlarda dünya çapında önemli çalışmalar yürüttüğünü, rakiplerine karşı üstünlük sağlayan ve maliyet açısından etkin ürünler geliştirdiğini ifade etti. Görgün, bu şirketlerin Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklarla işbirliği yapabileceği zeminleri uzun süredir değerlendirdiklerini belirterek, "Bunların olgunlaşacak ve hemen paylaşacağımız uygulama örnekleri de mevcut. Uzun vadede ortaya koyacağımız çalışmalar da mevcut." diye konuştu. Savunma sanayisindeki birikim sivil alanlara da aktarılıyor Savunma sanayisi sektörünün Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasındaki stratejik ilişkiler çerçevesinde uzun vadeli ekonomik ilişkilere katkı sunabileceğini ifade eden Görgün, sektörün yüksek teknolojinin üretildiği, rekabetin yoğun olduğu ve bilgi birikiminin yıllar içinde geliştirilerek ilerletildiği çok sayıda alanı ve disiplini barındırdığını söyledi. Görgün, savunma sanayisinde edinilen bilgi birikimiyle geliştirilen özgün tasarım ve ürünlerin yalnızca savunma ihtiyaçlarını karşılamakla sınırlı kalmadığını dile getirerek, bu çalışmaların zamanla sivil alanlarda da yerel ürün, platform ve çözümlerin geliştirilmesine imkan sağladığını kaydetti. Türkiye'de ve dünyada bunun çeşitli örneklerinin bulunduğunu belirten Görgün, savunma sanayisi şirketlerinin sağlık, enerji, ulaştırma ve şehir güvenliği alanlarında geliştirdiği çözümlerin hem Türkiye'de hem de yurt dışında kullanıldığını ifade etti. Görgün, bu tecrübeye dayalı modelleri Suudi Arabistanlı muhataplarıyla da paylaştıklarını aktararak, iki ülke arasındaki işbirliğinin savunma sanayisinin yanı sıra farklı sektörlere de katkı sunabileceğini bildirdi. "Dört binin üzerinde ana yüklenici ve KOBİ'den oluşan bir ekosistemimiz var" Türkiye'nin savunma sanayisinde geniş bir üretim ve tedarik ekosistemine sahip olduğuna dikkati çeken Görgün, ana yükleniciler ve KOBİ'lerle birlikte sektörde faaliyet gösteren şirket sayısının 4 binin üzerinde olduğunu belirtti. Görgün, bu ekosistemin koordinasyon içinde çalışmasının önemine işaret ederek, Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığı aracılığıyla şirketler arasındaki işleyişi koordine ettiklerini, tedarik zincirinin güçlendirilmesi ve kırılganlıkların önlenmesi için gerekli yapılanmaları oluşturduklarını söyledi. Türkiye'nin bu alandaki tecrübesinin dost ve müttefik ülkeler tarafından da değer gördüğünü ifade eden Görgün, söz konusu birikimi paylaşmaya devam ettiklerini kaydetti. Görgün, İstanbul'da düzenlenen Türkiye-Suudi Arabistan Savunma Sanayii Günleri'nin de bu işbirliğinin somut sonuçlara dönüşmesine katkı sunacak bir platform olarak tasarlandığını belirterek, organizasyonun Türk ve Suudi Arabistanlı şirketler arasındaki etkileşimi artırmayı amaçladığını dile getirdi. Etkinliğin, SAHA İstanbul, Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığı ve Suudi Arabistan tarafından ise SAMI'nin katkılarıyla gerçekleştirildiğini aktaran Görgün, programın şirketler arasında işbirliği imkanlarının değerlendirildiği ve ikili iş görüşmeleriyle zenginleştirilen bir platforma dönüştürüldüğünü söyledi. "Son üç yılda 75'in üzerinde toplantı yaptık" Görgün, Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasında savunma sanayisi alanındaki temasların yoğun biçimde sürdüğünü vurgulayarak, "Son üç yılda bu kapsamda 75'in üzerinde toplantı gerçekleştirdik." dedi. Toplantıların önemli bir bölümüne kendisinin de katıldığını belirten Görgün, bu sayının iki ülkenin ekiplerinin, farklı takımlarının, enstitülerinin ve kurumlarının ayda ortalama iki kez bir araya geldiğini gösterdiğini ifade etti. Son olarak Görgün, yoğun temasların sonuçlarının hem iki ülke hem de bölge açısından olumlu ve faydalı olacağını değerlendirdi. DEİK, SAHA İstanbul ve SAMI şirketinin düzenlediği etkinliğe 100'den fazla Türk ve 25'ten fazla Suudi şirketi katıldı.

Gördün, Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığı aracılığıyla Türk şirketlerini Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklar ve yerel kapasiteyle buluşturacak programlar oluşturduklarını aktararak, bu alanda hayata geçirilmiş başarılı örneklerin bulunduğunu söyledi. Savunma sanayisinin yüksek teknolojiye dayalı ve geniş bir faaliyet alanına sahip olduğunu vurgulayan Görgün, Türk şirketlerinin farklı alanlarda dünya çapında önemli çalışmalar yürüttüğünü, rakiplerine karşı üstünlük sağlayan ve maliyet açısından etkin ürünler geliştirdiğini ifade etti. Görgün, bu şirketlerin Suudi Arabistan'daki yerel ortaklarla işbirliği yapabileceği zeminleri uzun süredir değerlendirdiklerini belirterek, "Bunların olgunlaşacak ve hemen paylaşacağımız uygulama örnekleri de mevcut. Uzun vadede ortaya koyacağımız çalışmalar da mevcut." diye konuştu. Savunma sanayisindeki birikim sivil alanlara da aktarılıyor Savunma sanayisi sektörünün Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasındaki stratejik ilişkiler çerçevesinde uzun vadeli ekonomik ilişkilere katkı sunabileceğini ifade eden Görgün, sektörün yüksek teknolojinin üretildiği, rekabetin yoğun olduğu ve bilgi birikiminin yıllar içinde geliştirilerek ilerletildiği çok sayıda alanı ve disiplini barındırdığını söyledi. Görgün, savunma sanayisinde edinilen bilgi birikimiyle geliştirilen özgün tasarım ve ürünlerin yalnızca savunma ihtiyaçlarını karşılamakla sınırlı kalmadığını dile getirerek, bu çalışmaların zamanla sivil alanlarda da yerel ürün, platform ve çözümlerin geliştirilmesine imkan sağladığını kaydetti. Türkiye'de ve dünyada bunun çeşitli örneklerinin bulunduğunu belirten Görgün, savunma sanayisi şirketlerinin sağlık, enerji, ulaştırma ve şehir güvenliği alanlarında geliştirdiği çözümlerin hem Türkiye'de hem de yurt dışında kullanıldığını ifade etti. Görgün, bu tecrübeye dayalı modelleri Suudi Arabistanlı muhataplarıyla da paylaştıklarını aktararak, iki ülke arasındaki işbirliğinin savunma sanayisinin yanı sıra farklı sektörlere de katkı sunabileceğini bildirdi. "Dört binin üzerinde ana yüklenici ve KOBİ'den oluşan bir ekosistemimiz var" Türkiye'nin savunma sanayisinde geniş bir üretim ve tedarik ekosistemine sahip olduğuna dikkati çeken Görgün, ana yükleniciler ve KOBİ'lerle birlikte sektörde faaliyet gösteren şirket sayısının 4 binin üzerinde olduğunu belirtti. Görgün, bu ekosistemin koordinasyon içinde çalışmasının önemine işaret ederek, Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığı aracılığıyla şirketler arasındaki işleyişi koordine ettiklerini, tedarik zincirinin güçlendirilmesi ve kırılganlıkların önlenmesi için gerekli yapılanmaları oluşturduklarını söyledi. Türkiye'nin bu alandaki tecrübesinin dost ve müttefik ülkeler tarafından da değer gördüğünü ifade eden Görgün, söz konusu birikimi paylaşmaya devam ettiklerini kaydetti. Görgün, İstanbul'da düzenlenen Türkiye-Suudi Arabistan Savunma Sanayii Günleri'nin de bu işbirliğinin somut sonuçlara dönüşmesine katkı sunacak bir platform olarak tasarlandığını belirterek, organizasyonun Türk ve Suudi Arabistanlı şirketler arasındaki etkileşimi artırmayı amaçladığını dile getirdi. Etkinliğin, SAHA İstanbul, Savunma Sanayii Başkanlığı ve Suudi Arabistan tarafından ise SAMI'nin katkılarıyla gerçekleştirildiğini aktaran Görgün, programın şirketler arasında işbirliği imkanlarının değerlendirildiği ve ikili iş görüşmeleriyle zenginleştirilen bir platforma dönüştürüldüğünü söyledi. "Son üç yılda 75'in üzerinde toplantı yaptık" Görgün, Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasında savunma sanayisi alanındaki temasların yoğun biçimde sürdüğünü vurgulayarak, "Son üç yılda bu kapsamda 75'in üzerinde toplantı gerçekleştirdik." dedi. Toplantıların önemli bir bölümüne kendisinin de katıldığını belirten Görgün, bu sayının iki ülkenin ekiplerinin, farklı takımlarının, enstitülerinin ve kurumlarının ayda ortalama iki kez bir araya geldiğini gösterdiğini ifade etti. Son olarak Görgün, yoğun temasların sonuçlarının hem iki ülke hem de bölge açısından olumlu ve faydalı olacağını değerlendirdi. DEİK, SAHA İstanbul ve SAMI şirketinin düzenlediği etkinliğe 100'den fazla Türk ve 25'ten fazla Suudi şirketi katıldı.

news.titleTr: Altın fiyatlarında 'çok daha düşebilir' uyarısı: Para yön değiştiriyor
news.summaryTr: Sparta Portföy Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Taner Özarslan, küresel sermayenin yükselen faizlere yöneldiğini belirterek altın fiyatlarında düşüşün devam edebileceği uyarısında bulundu. Özarslan, yatırımcıların altındaki sert düşüşü tek başına alım fırsatı olarak görmemesi gerektiğini söyledi.
news.articleText: Altın fiyatlarında 'çok daha düşebilir' uyarısı: Para yön değiştiriyor Sparta Portföy Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Taner Özarslan, küresel sermayenin yükselen faizlere yöneldiğini belirterek altın fiyatlarında düşüşün devam edebileceği uyarısında bulundu. Özarslan, yatırımcıların altındaki sert düşüşü tek başına alım fırsatı olarak görmemesi gerektiğini söyledi. Sparta Portföy Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Taner Özarslan, CNBC-e ekranlarında yayınlanan Para Ekranı programında Şafak Tükle'nin sorularını yanıtladı. Altın fiyatlarındaki düşüşü değerlendiren Özarslan, küresel faiz beklentilerinin altın üzerinde baskı oluşturduğunu belirterek yatırımcılara uyarılarda bulundu. Altının hareketli bir yatırım aracı olduğunu belirten Özarslan, merkez bankalarının, fonların ve bireysel yatırımcıların altına olan talebinin fiyatlar üzerinde önemli rol oynadığını söyledi. Özarslan, fiyatlardaki düşüşün talep tarafına da olumsuz yansıdığına dikkat çekti. Altında talep daralması fiyatları etkiliyor Anadolu'daki yatırımcıların altınlarını bozdurarak elde ettikleri kazançlarla farklı yatırımlar yaptığını belirten Özarslan, altın alma sürecinin tersine döndüğünü ifade etti. Altın fiyatları açısından talep daralmasının önemli olduğunu vurgulayan Özarslan, düşüşün devam edebileceğini söyledi. Özarslan, yatırımcıların altının belirli bir seviyeye gerilemesini alım fırsatı olarak değerlendirmemesi gerektiğini belirterek, fiyatların seyrinde uluslararası dengelerin belirleyici olacağını kaydetti. Para altından faize yöneliyor Küresel piyasalarda paranın altından ziyade yükselen faizleri takip ettiğini belirten Özarslan, ABD'de üç faiz artırımı beklentisinin altına yönelik beklentileri zayıflattığını söyledi. Özarslan, "Altın mutlaka bir yerden döner ama önce nerede duracak? O yüzden düşen bıçağı yakalamak değil esas hedef" ifadelerini kullandı. "Altın çok düştü diye almak mantıklı değil" Yatırımcıların uluslararası sermayenin tercihlerini de dikkate alması gerektiğini belirten Özarslan, ABD tahvillerinin sunduğu yüzde 5 ve üzerindeki getirinin altına alternatif oluşturduğuna dikkat çekti. Özarslan, "Altın çok düştü diye almak mantıklı değil. Yükselebilir ama uluslararası bir yatırımcı olarak baktığınızda yüzde 5 ve üzeri getiri elde edebilen bir yatırımcının altın tarafına biraz daha soğuk bakacağını düşünüyorum" dedi.

news.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
news.summary: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
news.summaryTr: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
news.articleText: What we know about the global Microsoft outage - Published A major global Microsoft outage has caused problems, or in some cases disabled entire services, including emails and artificial intelligence products. Reports of problems with the email provider Outlook peaked globally at nearly 140,000 around 18:00 GMT on Thursday, according to monitoring website Downdetector. Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. Which services are affected? Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems". While customers are reporting varying levels of access - many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. Some users have been able to use Teams as normal and are using messaging and online meeting functions as usual. How many people have been affected? The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website. The software is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services. Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected. Government agencies and services, including the Singaporean government and Australia's spy agency, have also said they have been affected. Several GP practices across the UK have warned of potential problems, with some instructing patient to make urgent queries over the phone instead of by email or web form. What went wrong? Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to "elevated load" on its infrastructure. The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do. In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became "unexpectedly unavailable", the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these. On Friday morning, Microsoft said it had observed "marginal success" in its efforts to treat the incident. The company said in its latest update that is it continuing to monitor activity across regions to evaluate server status and determine what actions it can take to improve capacity. In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were "not taking as expected". What have experts said? Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. "Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. "Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said. Paul Spain from New Zealand-based advisory firm Gorilla Technology said that with e-mails and services offline, companies have practically "lost a business day", which is "frustrating" users". news.title: Dünyada bankacılık hizmetlerine erişim haritası: Türkiye'de oran yüzde 74,09
news.summary: World Population Review verilerine göre, Türkiye'de 15 yaş ve üzeri nüfusun yüzde 74,09'u bankacılık hizmetlerinden yararlanıyor. Bu oran erkeklerde yüzde 85,34, kadınlarda yüzde 62,55 olarak ölçülürken Danimarka ve İzlanda yüzde 100 ile ilk sırada yer alıyor.
